# AnkiDraft — Full Documentation Corpus (EN & FR)

Source: https://ankidraft.app

---

# [EN] AI Consultant and MCP Assistant Connection
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/consultant_mcp/
Description: Chat with the built-in AI Consultant or connect Claude Desktop and Cursor to AnkiDraft via MCP to query, audit, and enrich your decks safely.

The **AI Consultant** (<kbd>Ctrl+6</kbd>) is your interactive study assistant inside AnkiDraft. You can also control AnkiDraft from your favorite external AI client via the standard **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**.

## 1. What the AI Consultant Can Do

Ask in plain English:
- *"Find chapters in my cardiology textbook that don't have any flashcards yet"*
- *"Search for duplicate cards in my Anatomy deck and propose a merge"*
- *"Shorten the 10 longest flashcards in this deck following Wozniak's rules"*

## 2. Safety Safeguard: Two-Phase Human Validation

Neither the built-in AI Consultant nor an external MCP agent can modify or delete your cards without your explicit confirmation:
1. The assistant prepares proposed changes inside a **Staged Bundle**.
2. You inspect a clear before/after diff of every card added, edited, or deleted.
3. Click **Apply** or **Reject**: you remain in complete control of your collection.

## 3. Connecting External Clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.)

In **AI Consultant** > **MCP Server**, enable the local server and copy the configuration snippet in one click to let your external assistant query your decks and study documents safely.

---

# [EN] Configuring AI Providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/
Description: Securely connect your OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini API keys, configure local providers, and track your token budget per pipeline in AnkiDraft.

AnkiDraft is **provider-agnostic**: you are free to use the AI service of your choice or switch models depending on the task.

## 1. Supported Providers

In **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **AI Providers**, you can configure:
- **OpenAI** (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, etc.)
- **Google Gemini** (Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro)
- **Anthropic Claude** (Claude Sonnet, Claude Haiku)
- **Any OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint** (Mistral, OpenRouter, university server)
- **Ollama (100% Free & Offline)**: see [Using a Free Local Model with Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/).

## 2. API Key Security

- Your API keys are stored in your **operating system's secure keychain** (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service).
- Keys never pass through any middleman server: AnkiDraft connects directly from your computer to your chosen provider.
- Application logs automatically redact any secret key (`sk-*`, `AIza*`).

## 3. Token Budget Control

Before running a batch generation across a large textbook, AnkiDraft estimates the required token count and lets you set a strict per-run token cap to prevent unexpected API bills.

---

# [EN] Using a Free Local Model with Ollama
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/
Description: Generate atomic Anki flashcards 100% offline and for free on your own computer using local Ollama models with full privacy and zero API fees.

Prefer not to use paid cloud APIs, or studying confidential documents offline? AnkiDraft integrates natively with **Ollama**.

## 1. Install Ollama in 2 Minutes

1. Download and install Ollama from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com).
2. Open a terminal and pull a model suited to your computer's RAM:
   - **8 GB RAM**: `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` or `ollama pull qwen2.5:3b`
   - **16 GB+ RAM (e.g., Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4)**: `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` or `ollama pull mistral`

## 2. Enable Ollama in AnkiDraft

1. Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **AI Providers**.
2. Select **Ollama (Local)**: the default local endpoint `http://localhost:11434` is detected automatically.
3. Click **Refresh Models** and choose the model you just downloaded.
4. You can now generate and audit flashcards for free and completely offline!

---

# [EN] Exporting Your Decks to Anki (.apkg)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/anki-sync/export-apkg/
Description: Generate a clean, ready-to-study .apkg deck for Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile with stable IDs and without losing your review history.

Once your flashcards are created and reviewed in AnkiDraft, transfer them to Anki in seconds using the `.apkg` exporter.

## 1. Exporting a Deck or Selection

1. Press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> or click **Export (.apkg)** in the toolbar.
2. Pick the deck (or hierarchical sub-decks `Subject::Chapter`) to export.
3. Keep **Include media files** checked if your flashcards contain diagrams, images, or TTS audio.
4. Click **Export** and choose where to save the `.apkg` file.

## 2. Opening in Anki Without Resetting Your Progress

Double-click the generated `.apkg` file:
- Every card carries a **stable unique identifier (GUID)**.
- If you re-export a deck after fixing a typo in AnkiDraft, Anki updates the card text **while keeping your FSRS / SM-2 scheduling history completely intact** (intervals, due dates, ease factor).
- Card color flags and suspended status are also preserved.

---

# [EN] Importing a Deck (.apkg) or Collection (.colpkg)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/anki-sync/import-colpkg/
Description: Load your existing Anki .apkg or .colpkg decks into AnkiDraft to enrich notes, audit card quality, and track textbook coverage across chapters.

Already using Anki for months or years? You can bring your existing flashcards into AnkiDraft anytime.

## 1. Opening the Import Wizard (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd>)

Press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> and drop your file: AnkiDraft automatically detects whether it is an `.apkg` deck package or a full `.colpkg` collection archive.

## 2. Difference Between `.apkg` and `.colpkg`

- **`.apkg` Deck Package (Incremental Merge)**: adds flashcards shared by a classmate or updates a specific deck without touching the rest of your collection.
- **`.colpkg` Collection Archive (Full Sync from Anki)**: aligns all your decks, note types, and review counters with your current Anki collection while preserving your PDFs, settings, and AI assistants inside AnkiDraft.

For a visual walkthrough of how AnkiDraft and Anki work together, read the [Visual Guide to the Distributed Lifecycle](/en/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/).

---

# [EN] Synchronization, Duplicates, and Smart Merge
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/anki-sync/synchro_smart_merge/
Description: Resolve conflicts during Anki imports with Smart Merge, preserve existing review schedules, and clean up duplicate flashcards automatically.

When collaborating on a shared deck or editing a flashcard in both Anki and AnkiDraft, **Smart Merge** protects your work.

## 1. How Smart Merge Works on `.apkg` Import

When an incoming flashcard shares the same identifier as an existing card in AnkiDraft:
- **If only review statistics changed in Anki**: no conflict is raised and the update happens seamlessly.
- **If the card text was edited on both sides**: a 3-pane comparison dialog (*Local Version*, *Common Base*, *Incoming Version*) lets you pick which wording to keep or combine both.

## 2. Finding and Merging Duplicates

From the Editor or through the AI Consultant, scan your decks for duplicates:
- **Exact duplicates**: flashcards sharing the exact same front field.
- **Near-duplicates**: flashcards phrased slightly differently that test the same definition, detected rapidly with built-in similarity matching.

---

# [EN] Generating Flashcards with AI
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/ai-generation/
Description: Automatically turn textbook chapters and lecture notes into atomic Q&A or cloze flashcards with structured AI pipelines and human validation.

AnkiDraft helps you rapidly turn dense study chapters into atomic flashcards while keeping you in full control through human staging review.

## 1. Starting a Batch Generation

1. Open the **Generation** view (<kbd>Ctrl+4</kbd>) or click **Generate Cards** from any document.
2. Select the course sections to process in the **Batch Slice Composer**:
   - **Direct Mode**: each checked section creates one generation task.
   - **Automatic Mode**: groups or splits sections automatically based on length.
3. Choose the target note type (*Basic Front/Back*, *Cloze Deletion*) and destination Anki deck.
4. Press <kbd>Ctrl+Enter</kbd> to start generation.

## 2. Tailoring Card Style (Personas)

Adapt the AI extraction style to your discipline:
- **Sciences & Medicine**: precise definitions, physiological mechanisms, reference values.
- **Law & Humanities**: core concepts, conceptual distinctions, dates, and case law.
- **Languages & Vocabulary**: contextual examples, idioms, and pronunciation notes.

## 3. Human Review Before Saving (Staging)

No AI-generated card is ever added blindly to your collection: all proposals land in the **Staging Review** queue where you can accept, edit, or reject each card in one click.

---

# [EN] Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Audio Cards
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/audio-tts/
Description: Automatically generate natural offline audio pronunciation for language and terminology flashcards using Kokoro or Piper neural TTS voices locally.

When studying foreign languages, medical terminology, or music, attaching an audio clip to a flashcard dramatically boosts retention.

## 1. Generating Field Pronunciation in One Click

1. In the Note Editor, place your cursor inside the field containing the word or sentence to pronounce.
2. Click the **Text-to-Speech (TTS)** icon in the toolbar.
3. Select the target language and natural voice (English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Mandarin, etc.).
4. The audio file is generated, normalized, and attached automatically as `[sound:filename.mp3]`, ready for Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile.

## 2. Batch Audio Generation

Have an entire vocabulary deck without audio? Select multiple cards in the editor table and run **Batch TTS Generation**: AnkiDraft generates audio for all selected cards in the background.

---

# [EN] Generation Pipelines and Smart Coverage
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/dag_et_rag/
Description: Automate multi-step flashcard creation with DAG pipelines and fill knowledge gaps across your textbooks using local RAG and Smart Coverage tools.

For large textbooks and courses, AnkiDraft combines two engines: **Generation Pipelines** (DAG workflows) and **Smart Coverage** (local RAG alignment).

## 1. Automating Multi-Step Workflows (DAG Pipelines)

A pipeline chains multiple steps automatically across your selected chapters:
1. **Retrieve key passages** from your course material.
2. **Extract flashcards** matching your target note type.
3. **Run automatic quality checks** (filtering overly long cards) and **TTS audio generation**.
4. **Queue cards for human staging review** before saving.

## 2. Spotting Uncovered Chapters (Smart Coverage)

Using local semantic indexing and provenance links (`NoteChunkLinkModel`), AnkiDraft compares your existing flashcards against your entire course:
- It highlights sections that have zero flashcards yet.
- You can ask the AI to **generate only the missing cards** without duplicating concepts you have already covered.

---

# [EN] Note Editor, KaTeX Math, and Cloze Deletions
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/editeur_notes_katex/
Description: Write and format Anki flashcards with live KaTeX math preview, cloze deletions, rich media attachments, and full per-note revision history in AnkiDraft.

The AnkiDraft Note Editor (<kbd>Ctrl+2</kbd>) provides a fast writing environment with real-time Anki card preview.

## 1. Writing Math and Chemistry Formulas (KaTeX)

AnkiDraft renders your LaTeX equations live without waiting for an Anki export:
- **Inline formula**: wrap your expression in `\( ... \)` or `$ ... $` (e.g., `$E = mc^2$`).
- **Centered block formula**: use `\[ ... \]` or `$$ ... $$`.
- **LaTeX Autocompletion**: type `\` followed by the first letters of a symbol (`\alpha`, `\frac`, `\sum`) to open the completion popup.

## 2. Creating Cloze Deletions

Cloze cards are great for memorizing precise definitions or short lists:
1. Highlight the word or phrase you want to hide.
2. Click the **Cloze** toolbar button to wrap it in `{{c1::your text}}`.
3. Add an optional hint using `{{c1::answer::hint}}`.

## 3. Revision History (Time Machine)

Edited a card by mistake? Every save (<kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd>) stores a local snapshot in the note history so you can compare and restore previous wording in one click.

---

# [EN] Quality Audit and Wozniak's 20 Rules
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/linter_wozniak/
Description: Detect and split overloaded, vague, or hard-to-remember flashcards with the Wozniak 20-Rules Linter to boost long-term Anki retention daily.

A poorly formulated flashcard (too long, testing multiple facts at once, or lacking context) quickly turns into a "leech" that you repeatedly fail in Anki.

AnkiDraft includes a built-in **Pedagogical Linter** based on **Piotr Wozniak's 20 rules of formulating knowledge** (creator of SuperMemo).

## 1. What the Quality Audit Checks

In the **Quality & Audit** view (<kbd>Ctrl+5</kbd>) or right inside the editor, AnkiDraft scores each card and highlights:
- **Information overload (non-atomicity)**: answers exceeding the recommended word threshold or mixing several independent facts.
- **Vague or ambiguous prompts**: open-ended questions like *"Describe..."* where the expected answer is unclear.
- **Blind enumerations**: lists of more than 3 or 4 items that are difficult to recall in order.
- **Overly broad cloze deletions**: cloze tags hiding an entire sentence instead of a single key concept.

## 2. Splitting Complex Cards in One Click

When a card is flagged as overloaded, click **Split into Atomic Cards**: the assistant proposes breaking it down into 2 or 3 short, focused flashcards that are much easier to retain long-term.

---

# [EN] Note Types, Templates, and CSS Styling
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/cards/note-types-and-templates/
Description: Customize Front/Back and Cloze note types, Jinja2 card templates, and responsive CSS visual styling for Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile.

AnkiDraft supports all standard Anki note types and lets you customize their visual layout.

## 1. Built-In Note Types

- **Basic (Front / Back)**: a focused question on the front, the answer and optional lecture notes on the back.
- **Basic (and reversed card)**: automatically generates cards in both directions (ideal for bilingual vocabulary).
- **Cloze Deletion**: hides one or more key terms `{{c1::...}}` inside a context sentence.

## 2. Customizing Fields and CSS

Add custom fields (e.g., *Source*, *Mnemonic*, *Audio*, *Diagram*) and tweak the card CSS stylesheet with instant preview in both light and dark modes.

## 3. Smart Note Type Reconciliation on Import

When you import an `.apkg` deck whose note type already exists in your collection, AnkiDraft automatically matches it instead of cluttering your collection with duplicate note types (`Basic-12345`).

---

# [EN] Installing AnkiDraft
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/installation/
Description: Download, install, and update AnkiDraft on macOS, Windows, and Linux from the latest official GitHub release with Ed25519 signature verification.

AnkiDraft is a standalone desktop application. You do not need to install Python or any developer tools on your computer.

## 1. Download the Installer (Latest Release)

Visit the [AnkiDraft homepage](https://ankidraft.app/en/#download) or go straight to the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/releases/latest) to automatically fetch the package for your system:

| Operating System | Published Formats (`releases/latest`) | System Requirements |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **macOS** | Disk image `.dmg` (Apple Silicon) or `.zip` archive | macOS 13 (Ventura) or newer, Apple Silicon chip (M1/M2/M3/M4) |
| **Windows** | Standalone `.exe` installer or portable `.zip` archive | Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit) |
| **Linux** | Portable `.AppImage` executable or `.tar.gz` archive | Modern 64-bit Linux distribution (Ubuntu 22.04+, Fedora, Arch) |

## 2. Step-by-Step Setup

### On macOS
1. Double-click the `.dmg` disk image downloaded from the [latest release](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/releases/latest).
2. Drag the application icon into your **Applications** folder.
3. Launch the app from Launchpad or Spotlight.

### On Windows
1. If you download the `.exe` installer, double-click it and follow the wizard (no administrator rights required for a user-level installation).
2. If you download the portable `.zip` archive, extract it and run the main executable.

### On Linux (AppImage)
1. Make the downloaded `.AppImage` file executable:
   ```bash
   chmod +x *.AppImage
   ```
2. Launch the application by double-clicking it or executing it in your terminal.

## 3. Where Is Your Data Stored?

All your study data stays locally on your drive inside `~/.ankidraft/profiles/<profile_name>/`:
- `ankidraft.db`: your local SQLite database of cards, documents, and history.
- `media/`: images and audio clips attached to your flashcards.

## 4. Automatic Updates

AnkiDraft automatically checks for official releases and verifies both the cryptographic signature (Ed25519) and SHA-256 checksum before installing any update.

---

# [EN] Interface Overview
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/interface-overview/
Description: Take a guided tour of AnkiDraft workspaces, 4 switchable window layouts (IDE, macOS, Dashboard, Glass), and 12 built-in visual themes for study.

AnkiDraft is designed to stay clean and responsive whether you work on a laptop screen or an ultrawide monitor.

## 1. Main Workspaces

Switch between workspaces from the sidebar or with keyboard shortcuts <kbd>Ctrl+1</kbd> through <kbd>Ctrl+6</kbd>:

- **Dashboard (<kbd>Ctrl+1</kbd>)**: overview of your decks, document coverage progress, and recent activity.
- **Editor & Browser (<kbd>Ctrl+2</kbd>)**: manual creation, editing with live KaTeX math preview, cloze deletions, and card management.
- **Documents & Sources (<kbd>Ctrl+3</kbd>)**: library of your PDFs, YouTube videos, audio recordings, and web articles with per-chapter coverage bars.
- **Generation & Pipelines (<kbd>Ctrl+4</kbd>)**: batch flashcard creation across selected chapters.
- **Quality & Wozniak Audit (<kbd>Ctrl+5</kbd>)**: detection of overloaded, vague, or hard-to-memorize flashcards.
- **AI Consultant (<kbd>Ctrl+6</kbd>)**: conversational assistant that inspects your decks and prepares staged improvements for your approval.

## 2. Command Palette (<kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd>)

Press <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> anytime to open the global command palette: type a few letters to jump to a view, trigger an `.apkg` export, open a user guide, or change a setting without leaving the keyboard.

## 3. Customizing Layouts and Themes

In **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Appearance**:
- Pick from **4 interchangeable layouts** (*IDE Studio*, *macOS Native*, *Dashboard*, *Glassmorphism*) using high-resolution preview cards.
- Choose from **12 color themes** (light and dark) crafted for long study sessions.

# [EN] Managing Profiles and Your Collection
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/profiles-and-workspaces/
Description: Create isolated study profiles in AnkiDraft, manage per-profile SQLite databases and media folders, and protect your local data with backups.

AnkiDraft lets you completely isolate multiple collections using **user profiles**.

## 1. Why Use Multiple Profiles?

Each profile has its own SQLite database and dedicated media folder (images, audio):
- Create separate profiles for distinct fields of study (e.g., *Medical School*, *Bar Exam*, *Japanese*).
- Share a computer between multiple people without ever mixing flashcards or documents.

## 2. Creating or Switching Profiles

1. Open the profile selector from the application header or at startup.
2. Click **New Profile** and give it a clear name.
3. Switch between profiles in one click: AnkiDraft automatically locks the active profile to prevent concurrent write conflicts.

## 3. Automatic Backups

Before any sensitive operation (such as replacing your collection from a `.colpkg` archive or applying an update), AnkiDraft automatically creates a timestamped backup of your local database inside your profile folder.

---

# [EN] Quickstart Guide
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/getting-started/quickstart/
Description: Create, review, and export your first Anki flashcard deck in 5 minutes with AnkiDraft, and pick the step-by-step workflow tailored to your subject.

This guide walks you through creating your first Anki flashcard deck in minutes and helps you pick the end-to-end workflow that matches your study material and AI setup.

## Which workflow fits your goal?

Jump straight to the recipe built for your use case:

1. **[Medicine & STEM: Dense PDFs, KaTeX Math, and Diagrams](/en/workflows/medecine-sciences-pdf/)** — scope textbook chapters, extract formulas and figures, and audit against Wozniak rules (Studio or MCP).
2. **[Languages & Audio: Vocabulary and Offline TTS Pronunciation](/en/workflows/langues-et-audio-tts/)** — add natural offline Kokoro or Piper voice audio and fix ambiguous cards via MCP.
3. **[YouTube Video & Audio Lectures: Transcription and Extraction](/en/workflows/cours-video-youtube-audio/)** — transcribe recorded lectures with Whisper or subtitles and turn key segments into cards.
4. **[Zero API Key Workflow with an External MCP Agent](/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/)** — drive AnkiDraft directly from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or Antigravity without extra API costs.
5. **[Anki Collection Rescue & Hygiene (Studio & MCP)](/en/workflows/sauvetage-et-hygiene-anki-mcp/)** — import your `.colpkg` safely, eliminate duplicates and leeches, run MCP audit campaigns, and export back without losing SRS history.

## Built-in Creation Studio vs. External MCP Agent

AnkiDraft works either standalone in the Creation Studio or connected to your existing AI assistant over MCP.

| Dimension | Built-in Creation Studio | External Agent via MCP Server |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AI setup required** | Free local model (Ollama) or API key (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) | Existing plan (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, Antigravity) — **zero API key** |
| **Interaction style** | Visual chapter picker, prebuilt DAG pipelines, one-click tools | Natural conversation in your AI client connected on port `8765` |
| **Best suited for** | Batch PDF extraction, bulk TTS generation, visual KaTeX editing | Cross-deck gap audits, multi-step hygiene campaigns, note-type refactoring |
| **Human control** | **Staging Review** queue before saving | **Safeguard (Two-Phase Commit)**: nothing changes until you click **Apply** |

## The 4-Step Core Flow (Studio)

### Step 1: Select or Create Your Profile

On first launch, AnkiDraft opens the `default` profile. To keep subjects isolated (e.g., *Medicine*, *Languages*), click the profile selector at the bottom of the sidebar to create a dedicated workspace.

### Step 2: Configure an AI Provider (Optional)

Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) and switch to **AI Engines**:
- **100% free & offline**: install [Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/) locally and choose a model.
- **Cloud API key**: enter your OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude key (stored in your OS encrypted keychain).
- **Zero API key**: enable the [Local MCP Server](/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/) to work with Claude or Cursor.

### Step 3: Import Your First Document

1. Open the **My Documents** view (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>) from the sidebar.
2. Drag and drop a PDF, Word, PowerPoint, or EPUB file, or paste a YouTube lecture URL.
3. Select the chapters you want to study, then switch to **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>) and click **Generate** (or **Forge Section**).

### Step 4: Validate and Export to Anki

Review generated cards, run the [Wozniak Quality Audit](/en/cards/linter_wozniak/) (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>), then press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> (**Export Anki Cards (.apkg)**). Double-click the exported `.apkg` file to add your cards directly into Anki for daily spaced-repetition review.

> Want plain-language definitions with concrete Before / After examples? Read the [User Glossary](/en/guides/glossaire/).

# [EN] Visual Guide to the Distributed Lifecycle (AnkiDraft & Anki)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/
Description: Understand how the AnkiDraft authoring studio and the Anki spaced-repetition engine work together via .apkg and .colpkg without sync conflicts.

Welcome to the distributed workflow guide for AnkiDraft (formerly AnkiForge).

AnkiDraft and Anki work hand in hand as complementary tools:
- **AnkiDraft is your Authoring Studio**: your AI-assisted workspace where you organize textbooks, track chapter coverage (Smart Coverage / Cycle Global Distribué), design flashcards, and validate card quality.
- **Anki is your Spaced Repetition Engine (SRS)**: the application dedicated to your daily reviews. Anki holds exclusive authority over your review intervals, due dates, and spaced repetition algorithms (FSRS or SM-2).

Thanks to this strict boundary (**Sanctuarisation**), **you never risk losing your review progress in Anki or overwriting your study documents and AI models in AnkiDraft**.

---

## 1. The Global Workflow Cycle

The diagram below illustrates the workflow between creating cards in AnkiDraft and reviewing them in Anki:

1. **AnkiDraft Studio**: Import your study sources (PDF, articles, videos, audio lectures). The studio segments the text and tracks your chapter coverage.
2. **Staging Review**: Every generated flashcard goes through human validation and receives a permanent unique identifier (GUID).
3. **Export to Anki (.apkg)**: Export your new cards as an `.apkg` package and open it in Anki.
4. **Periodic Refresh (.colpkg)**: Review daily in Anki. Periodically export your `.colpkg` collection from Anki and drop it into AnkiDraft to refresh your retention statistics and sync card deletions.

---

## 2. Data Boundary: Studio Scope vs. Anki Scope (Sanctuarisation)

### 🛡️ Studio Scope (Strictly Preserved)
Never overwritten when you import an Anki collection:
- Original documents (PDFs, transcripts, Markdown files, image plates).
- Local semantic indexes and coverage links.
- AI personas, prompts, and generation pipelines.
- Application settings, themes, and custom shortcuts.

### 🗂️ Anki Collection Scope (Synchronized & Replaced)
Reflects your exact Anki collection:
- Decks and hierarchical sub-decks.
- Note types, Front/Back templates, and CSS styles.
- Notes, physical cards, flags, and SRS review counters.

---

## 3. Which Archive Format Should You Choose: .apkg or .colpkg?

| Criterion | Deck Package (`.apkg`) | Collection Archive (`.colpkg`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Purpose** | Share or add new/updated flashcards | Full replacement for exact alignment with Anki |
| **Behavior** | **Incremental merge**: adds or updates cards without touching other decks | **Full Anki scope replacement**: matches your Anki collection state |
| **Deletions** | Never deletes existing local cards | **Purges cards deleted in Anki (prevents Zombies)** |
| **Safety** | Smart Merge conflict dialog | **Automatic SQLite backup created before replacement** |

---

## 4. Typical Study Session Timeline

---

## 5. Preventing Zombie Cards (Zombies) and Empty Fronts

### 🧟 1. Eradicating Zombie Cards (Zombies)
When you delete an obsolete card in Anki and later import a `.colpkg` archive into AnkiDraft, the deleted card is permanently removed from AnkiDraft so it never reappears in future exports.

### 📄 2. Official Anki Non-Empty Front Rule
AnkiDraft evaluates conditional templates (`{{#Field}}...{{/Field}}` and `{{^Field}}...{{/Field}}`): if the rendered front of a card is empty, no physical card is created.

---

# [EN] FAQ and Troubleshooting
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/faq_depannage/
Description: Find answers to frequently asked questions and step-by-step troubleshooting for AnkiDraft installation, Ollama, PDF OCR, and Anki .apkg exports.

Find answers to the most common questions about AnkiDraft.

## 1. General Questions

### Does AnkiDraft replace Anki?
No—AnkiDraft and Anki complement each other. **AnkiDraft** is the authoring and quality-auditing studio where you turn textbooks and lectures into atomic flashcards, while **Anki** (Desktop, AnkiWeb, AnkiMobile, AnkiDroid) is the spaced-repetition engine where you do your daily reviews.

### Can I use AnkiDraft for free and offline?
Yes. AnkiDraft is free, runs offline on your computer, and supports free local AI models via [Ollama](/en/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/) without any paid API subscription.

### Are my PDFs and flashcards uploaded to the cloud?
No. Your PDFs, SQLite database, and media files stay locally on your drive (`~/.ankidraft/`). If you configure a cloud AI provider (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude), only the text passages you explicitly select for card generation are sent directly to your API account.

## 2. Troubleshooting

### macOS shows a security prompt on first launch
Make sure you dragged **AnkiDraft** into your **Applications** folder from the `.dmg` disk image. If macOS asks for confirmation on first open, right-click the **AnkiDraft** icon and select **Open**.

### My math formulas do not render in Anki
Verify that your equations use standard MathJax/KaTeX delimiters (`\( ... \)` for inline math and `\[ ... \]` for centered block equations).

### How do I report a bug or request a feature?
Inside AnkiDraft, open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Help** > **Report an Idea or Bug**, or open an issue on the [official GitHub repository](https://github.com/Skyl9/AnkiDraft/issues).

---

# [EN] User Glossary: Key AnkiDraft Concepts Explained Simply
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/glossaire/
Description: Understand every core AnkiDraft concept (Wozniak rules, Cloze, Smart Coverage, DAG, RAG, MCP, Safeguard) with clear Before / After study examples.

AnkiDraft combines spaced-repetition best practices with local AI tools. This glossary explains every technical term in plain English, paired with a concrete **Before / After** example.

---

## 1. Atomic Knowledge & Wozniak's 20 Rules

A core principle from Piotr Wozniak (creator of SuperMemo): a great flashcard tests **one short, unambiguous fact** at a time (minimum information principle). AnkiDraft's linter automatically spots bloated or vague prompts.

- **Before**: *Front:* "Explain the Krebs cycle (steps, rate-limiting enzymes, ATP/NADH/FADH2 yield)." ➔ Too dense to grade honestly during reviews.
- **After**: 3 crisp, independent cards: (1) "Which enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting step of the Krebs cycle?", (2) "How many NADH molecules are produced per turn of the Krebs cycle?", (3) "Where in the cell does the Krebs cycle take place?".

---

## 2. Cloze Deletion

A fill-in-the-blank card (`{{c1::hidden term}}`) that hides one key word or phrase inside a clear sentence so you recall it directly in context (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd>).

- **Before**: "Define osmosis?" / "Movement of solvent across a semipermeable membrane from lower to higher solute concentration."
- **After**: "During osmosis, solvent moves across a semipermeable membrane from a {{c1::hypotonic (lower solute)}} solution to a {{c2::hypertonic (higher solute)}} solution."

---

## 3. Smart Coverage

A traceability tracker linking each generated card back to its exact source heading or page. It shows which chapters of your PDF already have flashcards and which sections are still uncovered.

- **Before**: Manually flipping through a 180-page textbook wondering whether you forgot subsection 3.4.
- **After**: The *Smart Coverage* gauge reports `Chapter 3: 82% covered — Section 3.4 (0 cards)` and lets you draft cards solely for that gap.

---

## 4. Scoping: Exclude vs. Neutralize

Two non-destructive actions to filter a textbook without deleting pages ([Scope & Chapters](/en/sources/scope-and-slices/)):
- **Exclude**: temporarily hides an off-syllabus chapter from AI generation.
- **Neutralize**: removes structural boilerplate (cover, table of contents, acknowledgments) from the *Smart Coverage* denominator.

- **Before**: A 300-page book with 30 pages of index and bibliography caps your coverage at 90% or generates useless cards about publisher copyrights.
- **After**: Index neutralized, bibliography excluded ➔ coverage accurately reaches **100% of active chapters** with zero junk cards.

---

## 5. Generation Pipeline (DAG)

An automated multi-step workflow (e.g., retrieve key passages ➔ synthesize clean Markdown ➔ draft cards ➔ add TTS audio ➔ stage for human review).

- **Before**: Copying a chapter into a chat box, generating cards, fixing broken LaTeX manually, then creating audio one card at a time.
- **After**: Clicking **Run Pipeline** executes the full workflow automatically and delivers clean drafts ready to review.

---

## 6. Local Semantic Search (RAG)

100% local indexing on your computer that lets AI retrieve relevant sections of your textbooks by **meaning** (not just exact keywords) before drafting or auditing cards.

- **Before**: Stuffing an entire textbook into a prompt (slow, expensive, and prone to hallucinations).
- **After**: Local RAG pulls only the 3 paragraphs relevant to the concept and keeps exact page provenance.

---

## 7. MCP Server (Model Context Protocol)

An open standard built into AnkiDraft that lets your external AI assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity) read your courses and decks locally with zero extra API keys.

- **Before**: Copy-pasting notes back and forth between Anki, PDFs, and a browser chat window.
- **After**: Asking Claude directly *"Audit my Cardiology deck and draft missing cards for Chapter 4"* queries AnkiDraft live.

---

## 8. Safeguard & Staged Bundle (Two-Phase Human Approval)

A mandatory safety buffer: no AI proposal (create, edit, split, or delete) ever modifies your database directly. Every change enters a **Staged Bundle** with a Before / After diff until you click **Apply**.

- **Before**: Worrying that an automated prompt or script might accidentally overwrite 200 cards.
- **After**: You inspect every proposed card change side-by-side in the Safeguard and stay in 100% control.

---

## 9. Domain Gap Diagnosis & the 3 Cognitive Pathologies

A neuro-symbolic audit (`diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`) scanning all your decks together against a study topic to catch 3 pathologies:
- **Type 1 (Missing concepts)**: textbook concepts with zero matching flashcards.
- **Type 2 (Non-atomicity)**: bloated multi-fact cards needing splitting.
- **Type 3 (Bilingual glue)**: two languages mixed awkwardly in one card or bare word translations lacking context.

- **Before**: Realizing right before finals that 3 core topics are missing or scattered across unrelated decks.
- **After**: The audit collects related orphan cards across decks and pinpoints exact gaps and splits needed.

---

## 10. Studio Scope vs. Anki Collection Scope (`.apkg` vs. `.colpkg`)

AnkiDraft isolates authoring assets (**Studio Scope**: PDFs, transcripts, RAG indexes, prompts) from synced cards (**Anki Collection Scope**).
- `.apkg`: adds or merges a targeted deck.
- `.colpkg`: mirrors your complete Anki collection (removes cards deleted in Anki while keeping all PDFs intact).

- **Before**: Importing a full Anki backup risked wiping study notes or resurrecting deleted cards ("zombie cards").
- **After**: `.colpkg` sync updates your collection cleanly while keeping Studio sources safe and preventing zombie cards ([Distributed Lifecycle Guide](/en/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/)).

---

## 11. Smart Merge

A 3-way visual diff (**Local**, **Common Base**, **Incoming**) inspired by developer merge tools: when importing an updated `.apkg` from a classmate, only true text conflicts require your decision.

- **Before**: Blindly overwriting your personal edits or losing a teammate's additions when importing a shared deck.
- **After**: Pick the exact version per field while preserving media and review scheduling.

---

## 12. Leech Card

Anki's term for a card you repeatedly fail during reviews—almost always because it is too verbose, poorly phrased, or interferes with a sibling card.

- **Before**: Seeing the same frustrating card fail 8 times a month without sticking.
- **After**: AnkiDraft spots leeches from synced lapse counters and suggests splitting or clarifying them with distinctive cues.

---

# [EN] Keyboard Shortcuts Reference
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/guides/raccourcis_clavier/
Description: Official reference of all keyboard shortcuts in AnkiDraft by category and scope to navigate workspaces, edit cards, and run AI pipelines fast.

This page lists the default keyboard shortcuts in AnkiDraft. You can customize any shortcut in **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Keyboard**.

> On macOS, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> maps automatically to <kbd>Cmd ⌘</kbd>.

## 1. Global Application Actions

| Action | Default Shortcut | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Command Palette** | <kbd>Ctrl+K</kbd> | `Application` | Open the global command palette omnibox |
| **Settings** | <kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd> | `Application` | Open the Settings dialog |
| **Save** | <kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd> | `Application` | Save changes in the active view |
| **Run Primary Action** | <kbd>Ctrl+Return</kbd> | `Application` | Trigger the main action in the active view (generate, run) |
| **Find / Search** | <kbd>Ctrl+F</kbd> | `Application` | Focus the search field in the active view |
| **Import Anki Package (.apkg / .colpkg)** | <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> | `Application` | Open the collection or deck import wizard |
| **Export Anki Cards (.apkg)** | <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> | `Application` | Open the `.apkg` card export dialog |
| **Interactive Guided Tour** | <kbd>F1</kbd> | `Application` | Launch the interactive feature tour |

## 2. Workspace Navigation

| Action | Default Shortcut | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dashboard** | <kbd>Ctrl+1</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Dashboard view |
| **Editor & Browser** | <kbd>Ctrl+2</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Note Editor and Card Browser |
| **Documents & Sources** | <kbd>Ctrl+3</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Document Hub |
| **Generation & Pipelines** | <kbd>Ctrl+4</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to Batch AI Generation |
| **Quality & Wozniak Audit** | <kbd>Ctrl+5</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the Wozniak Quality Linter |
| **AI Consultant** | <kbd>Ctrl+6</kbd> | `Application` | Switch to the interactive AI Consultant |

## 3. Note Editor & Formatting

| Action | Default Shortcut | Scope | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **New Note** | <kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd> | `View` | Create a new flashcard note |
| **Duplicate Note** | <kbd>Ctrl+D</kbd> | `View` | Duplicate the selected note |
| **Delete Note** | <kbd>Delete</kbd> | `View` | Delete the selected note(s) |
| **Bold** | <kbd>Ctrl+B</kbd> | `Widget` | Toggle bold text formatting |
| **Italic** | <kbd>Ctrl+I</kbd> | `Widget` | Toggle italic text formatting |
| **Underline** | <kbd>Ctrl+U</kbd> | `Widget` | Toggle underline formatting |
| **Insert Cloze Deletion** | <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd> | `Widget` | Wrap selection in `{{c1::...}}` |
| **Undo / Redo** | <kbd>Ctrl+Z</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+Z</kbd> | `Widget` | Undo or redo the last edit |

# [EN] Document Hub and Multimodal Formats
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/hub_multimodal/
Description: Overview of all supported study sources in AnkiDraft (PDF, YouTube, audio, web, DOCX, EPUB) with local-first parsing and source traceability.

The **Document Hub** centralizes all your study materials in one place and preserves a direct link between every flashcard and the exact paragraph it came from.

## 1. Supported Study Sources

| Source Type | Formats | What AnkiDraft Extracts |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **PDF Textbooks & Handouts** | `.pdf` | Chapter outline, text, tables, figures, and LaTeX math |
| **Online Videos** | YouTube URLs | Timestamped subtitles or local speech-to-text transcription |
| **Audio Recordings** | `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.m4a` | Paragraph-segmented transcript |
| **Web Articles** | `https://` URLs | Clean article body without ads or navigation clutter |
| **Office & Ebooks** | `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.epub`, `.md` | Heading hierarchy, lists, and slide notes |

## 2. Jump Back to the Source in One Click

While reviewing or editing any flashcard in the editor, click **View Source** to jump straight back to the corresponding chapter and paragraph in your original document.

---

# [EN] Importing PDFs, Slides, and Ebooks
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/import-pdf/
Description: Cleanly extract PDF textbooks, DOCX documents, PPTX slides, and EPUB books with Marker OCR, preserving diagrams, tables, and LaTeX formulas.

The AnkiDraft **Document Hub** turns static study files into structured chapters ready for flashcard generation.

## 1. Supported File Formats

Drag and drop directly into the **Documents** view:
- **PDF Documents (`.pdf`)**: lecture handouts, academic papers, and textbooks, preserving tables, figures, and LaTeX math equations.
- **Word Documents (`.docx`) and Slides (`.pptx`)**: extracts headings, bullet points, and speaker notes.
- **Ebooks (`.epub`) and Markdown / Plain Text (`.md`, `.txt`)**.

## 2. Choosing the PDF Extraction Mode

When importing a PDF, two extraction modes are available depending on your file:
- **Fast Standard Extraction**: best for clean digital PDFs where text is already selectable.
- **Advanced OCR & Math Recognition**: recommended for scanned handouts, multi-column layouts, or math-heavy courses.

## 3. Keeping Diagrams and Figures

Figures and diagrams extracted from your documents are automatically saved to your local media library so you can attach them to the front or back of any flashcard in one click.

---

# [EN] Importing Web Pages and Online Articles
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/import-web/
Description: Capture the core educational content of any online article or web documentation page into clean Markdown without ads, menus, or visual clutter.

Studying from online encyclopedias, technical blogs, or web courses? The AnkiDraft Web Importer extracts only the relevant study content.

## 1. Capturing a Web Page

1. In the **Documents** view, click **Import Web Page**.
2. Paste the article URL (`https://...`).
3. AnkiDraft automatically strips navigation menus, banners, and ads, keeping only headings, paragraphs, tables, code blocks, and illustrations.

## 2. Dynamic Web Pages

If a page requires JavaScript to render its content (single-page apps or interactive courses), enable **Full Browser Rendering** during import so AnkiDraft waits for the complete page text before extracting it.

# [EN] Importing YouTube Videos and Audio Lectures
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/import-youtube-audio/
Description: Turn any YouTube lecture, podcast, or classroom voice recording into timestamped transcripts and atomic Anki flashcards locally on your device.

AnkiDraft lets you build flashcards directly from online video lectures or recorded classroom sessions.

## 1. Importing a YouTube Video

1. Open the **Documents** view and click **Import from URL / YouTube**.
2. Paste the YouTube video link.
3. AnkiDraft immediately retrieves official or auto-generated subtitles and reconstructs a clean, timestamped transcript organized by topic.
4. If the video has no subtitles available, AnkiDraft can transcribe the audio stream locally.

## 2. Transcribing Audio Files (`.mp3`, `.wav`, `.m4a`)

Recorded a lecture or voice memo?
1. Drop your audio file into the **Documents** view.
2. Automatic transcription splits the recording into timestamped paragraphs.
3. Generate flashcards from the entire recording or pick only the key segments.

# [EN] Selecting Chapters and Tracking Coverage
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/sources/scope-and-slices/
Description: Choose which textbook sections or pages to study, exclude appendices non-destructively, and monitor your course coverage bar in real time today.

Textbooks and handouts often include a table of contents, preface, or bibliography that you do not want to turn into flashcards. AnkiDraft gives you fine-grained control over your study scope.

## 1. Three Exclusive Scope Modes

When preparing a flashcard generation batch, slice your document using one of three modes:
- **By Sections**: check specific sub-sections from the document outline.
- **By Pages**: specify a page range (e.g., pages 12 to 28).
- **By Chapters**: select whole chapters in a single click.

## 2. Excluding Out-of-Scope Sections

You can **exclude** non-essential sections such as prefaces or acknowledgments:
- Excluded sections are never deleted from your source document (you can re-enable them anytime).
- They are skipped during AI card generation and removed from your coverage denominator.

## 3. Monitoring Smart Coverage

Every flashcard generated from a course passage stays linked to its source section. In the **Documents** view, a visual progress bar shows which chapters are already covered by flashcards and which ones still need attention.

---

# [EN] YouTube Video & Audio Lectures: Transcription to Cards
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/workflows/cours-video-youtube-audio/
Description: Turn YouTube video lectures or classroom audio recordings into structured, atomic Anki flashcards using local transcription, slicing, and AI tools.

Recorded university lectures, YouTube explainers, and seminar audio files pack hours of spoken insight that are slow to review manually. This workflow turns speech into structured, atomic flashcards.

## 1. Import a YouTube URL or Local Audio Recording

1. Open **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>).
2. Choose your source type ([Import YouTube & Audio](/en/sources/import-youtube-audio/)):
   - **YouTube lecture**: click **Import from Web** and paste the video URL. AnkiDraft downloads official captions when present or falls back to local speech-to-text transcription.
   - **Recorded lecture or voice memo** (`.mp3`, `.wav`, `.m4a`, `.mp4`, `.ogg`): drag and drop the file into **My Documents**. Local **Whisper** transcription runs on your machine without uploading your recordings to third-party servers.

## 2. Turn Raw Transcripts into Structured Study Sections

Spoken transcripts naturally contain filler words, tangents, and broken sentences. Clean and outline the transcript before drafting flashcards:

- **In Creation Studio**: run a [DAG Pipeline](/en/cards/dag_et_rag/) with an upstream Markdown synthesis step before card extraction.
- **Via an MCP Agent**: ask Claude or Cursor to call `structure_transcript_for_ai` followed by `structure_document_sections` so timestamped speech becomes a crisp, hierarchical outline.

## 3. Slice by Topic and Generate Cards

1. Switch to **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>) or the **Batch Slice Composer** to process one thematic segment at a time.
2. Pick your note type (*Basic* or *Cloze*) and domain persona ([AI Card Generation](/en/cards/ai-generation/)).
3. Review every draft in **Staging** to catch spoken ambiguities or misheard technical terms before saving.

## 4. Automate Structuring and Drafting via MCP

When driving AnkiDraft from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or Cursor on port `8765` with zero extra API key:

- **MCP tools used**: `structure_transcript_for_ai`, `get_document_outline`, `create_notes_batch`, `begin_staged_bundle`, `commit_staged_bundle`.
- **Sample prompt**: *"Clean up raw transcript document #9 using `structure_transcript_for_ai` (didactic profile, keep timestamps), then stage atomic definitions and causal questions via `create_notes_batch` into deck `Lectures::Neuroscience` for Safeguard review."*

---

# [EN] Language Learning & Audio Workflow: Offline TTS Flashcards
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/workflows/langues-et-audio-tts/
Description: Build language vocabulary decks in AnkiDraft with offline neural text-to-speech audio (Kokoro or Piper), instant preview, and MCP batch enrichment.

This workflow shows how to build language decks (Japanese, Spanish, French, German, Mandarin, and more) with contextual sentence examples, 100% offline neural pronunciation audio, and clean bilingual formatting.

## 1. Bring In Your Vocabulary List or Study Material

You can start from any of three sources:
- A **source document** (grammar handout, vocabulary sheet, article, or subtitle file dropped into **My Documents**).
- An **existing Anki deck** imported with <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> ([Import .apkg / .colpkg](/en/anki-sync/import-colpkg/)).
- **Direct entry** inside **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>).

For higher long-term retention, prefer a **short contextual sentence** on the front card highlighting the target word rather than an isolated one-word translation.

## 2. Generate Offline Pronunciation Audio (Kokoro / Piper)

AnkiDraft supports local neural TTS engines that create standard `[sound:tts_xxx.mp3]` audio clips without internet access or cloud quotas ([Text-to-Speech & Audio](/en/cards/audio-tts/)):

1. Open **Settings** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Audio & TTS** and select a local engine (**Kokoro-82M** or **Piper ONNX**) along with the voice matching your target language.
2. **Single-card audio**: in **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>), click inside the target-language field and press the speaker/microphone button to synthesize and preview audio immediately.
3. **Batch deck audio**: select multiple notes in the browser and trigger **Batch TTS Generation** to synthesize missing audio clips in the background.

## 3. Enrich and Clean Up Language Decks via MCP

A frequent failure mode in language decks is **Type 3 Pathology (Bilingual Glue)**: cards mixing two languages in one prompt or pairing literal glosses with zero natural context. Your MCP agent can audit and fix this safely:

- **Add audio across an entire language deck**:
  - Tools used: `get_cards_by_deck_or_tag`, `generate_card_audio`, `generate_cards_batch_audio`.
  - Sample prompt: *"Fetch notes in deck `Languages::Japanese` (with `recursive=True`) missing `[sound:...]` tags and run `generate_cards_batch_audio` on the Expression field using a Japanese voice."*
- **Fix bilingual glue and add natural example sentences**:
  - Tools used: `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`, `propose_card_refactor`.
  - Sample prompt: *"Inspect `Languages::Spanish` with `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`, find cards with Type 3 bilingual glue or overloaded synonyms, and stage clean contextual rewrites via `propose_card_refactor`."*

## 4. Export with Deduplicated Audio Media

Press <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> to export your `.apkg`: AnkiDraft packages MD5-deduplicated audio files automatically so playback works smoothly on Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb, and AnkiMobile.

---

# [EN] Medicine & STEM Workflow: Dense PDFs, Math, and Diagrams
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/workflows/medecine-sciences-pdf/
Description: Step-by-step guide to turning dense medical or STEM textbook PDFs into atomic Anki flashcards complete with KaTeX math formulas, diagrams, and MCP.

This workflow shows how to turn dense university handouts or STEM textbooks (anatomy, physiology, physics, calculus) into atomic flashcards faithful to your source material, complete with KaTeX equations and labeled diagrams.

## 1. Import the PDF with Figure and Equation Extraction

1. Open **My Documents** (<kbd>Alt+7</kbd>) and click **Import File** (or drag and drop your `.pdf`).
2. Pick the extraction engine matching your file:
   - **Fast standard extraction** for clean digital PDFs without complex mathematical notation.
   - **Advanced OCR (Marker)** for scanned handouts, multi-column layouts, tables, and formulas converted into native LaTeX (`\(...\)` and `\[...\]`).
3. Extracted figures and anatomical plates are saved automatically to your local media library. See [Import PDFs, Slides, and Ebooks](/en/sources/import-pdf/) for details.

## 2. Scope Useful Chapters Without Deleting Source Pages

A 200-page course pack usually contains a preface, table of contents, and bibliography that distort generation and coverage tracking.

In the [Scope & Chapter Selector](/en/sources/scope-and-slices/):
- **Exclude** appendices, acknowledgments, and bibliographies: AI generation skips them while the original text remains intact.
- **Neutralize** the table of contents or cover pages: they are removed from your *Smart Coverage* denominator so your progress gauge stays accurate.

## 3. Generate Atomic Cards and Edit Math or Occlusions

1. Switch to **Creation Studio** (<kbd>Alt+2</kbd>) or open the **Batch Slice Composer** to split your selection by chapter.
2. Pick the target note type (*Basic*, *Cloze*, or *Image Occlusion*) and destination deck (e.g., `Medicine::Cardiology`).
3. In **Editor & Browser** (<kbd>Alt+3</kbd>), verify live KaTeX math rendering, turn key terms into cloze deletions with <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+C</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd+Shift+C</kbd> on macOS), or mask diagram labels ([Notes Editor & KaTeX](/en/cards/editeur_notes_katex/)).

## 4. Run a Wozniak Quality Check Before Export

Open **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>) to run the [Wozniak Quality Linter](/en/cards/linter_wozniak/): overloaded cards or multi-concept prompts are flagged for one-click splitting before exporting via <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> ([Export .apkg](/en/anki-sync/export-apkg/)).

## 5. Drive This Workflow via MCP (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity)

Prefer steering your exam preparation from Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or Cursor with zero extra API keys? Enable the local MCP server under **MCP Server & Agents** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>) and use these patterns:

- **Clean document scope before drafting**:
  - Tools used: `get_document_outline`, `exclude_document_region`, `neutralize_document_region`.
  - Sample prompt: *"Read the outline of document #4, neutralize the table of contents and exclude the bibliography, then list the active chapters."*
- **Find coverage gaps across decks and draft missing cards**:
  - Tools used: `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`, `search_document`, `create_notes_batch`.
  - Sample prompt: *"Run `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps` on the Action Potential chapter of my Physiology course across all decks, list Type 1 missing concepts, and stage atomic KaTeX flashcards `\( ... \)` for Safeguard review."*

> Every mutation proposed by an external MCP agent lands in the **Safeguard** review queue before touching your collection.

---

# [EN] Anki Collection Rescue: Duplicates, Leeches, and MCP Hygiene
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/workflows/sauvetage-et-hygiene-anki-mcp/
Description: Clean up an existing Anki collection (.colpkg): detect duplicates and leeches, run an MCP hygiene campaign, and split overloaded cards safely.

Stuck with an older Anki deck full of stubborn leeches, near-duplicate cards, messy tags, or bloated paragraphs? This workflow helps you rescue and normalize your collection without ever losing your spaced-repetition scheduling history (FSRS / SM-2).

## 1. Safely Import Your Anki Collection (`.colpkg`)

1. From Anki Desktop, export a full archive: **File > Export > Anki Collection Package (`.colpkg`)** including media and scheduling info.
2. In AnkiDraft, press <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> and drop your `.colpkg` file ([Import .apkg or .colpkg](/en/anki-sync/import-colpkg/)).
3. AnkiDraft automatically creates a backup SQLite snapshot and isolates your **Anki Collection Scope** from your **Studio Scope** (your PDFs, RAG indexes, and app settings remain untouched).

## 2. Spot Duplicates and Overloaded Cards in the Audit Hospital

1. Open **Analysis & AI Audit** (<kbd>Alt+4</kbd>).
2. Under **Audit & Wozniak Linter**, pick a deck and click **Run Audit**: verbose, ambiguous, or multi-concept cards receive targeted cognitive diagnostics ([Wozniak Linter](/en/cards/linter_wozniak/)).
3. Open **Merges & Duplicates** to detect near-identical notes with the native C Levenshtein matcher and resolve duplicates cleanly.

## 3. Run an Assisted Collection Hygiene Campaign via MCP

To clean hundreds of cards across multiple decks systematically, connect your MCP client (**Claude**, **Cursor**, **Antigravity**) on port `8765` and follow these four stages:

### Stage A — Fix Cards Flagged During Daily Reviews
While reviewing in Anki, flag painful cards (Red = split needed, Orange = fact-check), then re-import your `.colpkg` into AnkiDraft:
- **MCP tools**: `get_flagged_cards`, `get_note_full_profile_360`, `set_card_flag`.
- **Prompt**: *"Fetch all my red-flagged cards using `get_flagged_cards`, diagnose why they keep failing with `audit_card_wozniak`, and stage atomic rewrites for each."*

### Stage B — Break Down Deck Silos and Diagnose 3 Pathologies
- **MCP tools**: `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`, `diagnose_deck_weaknesses`, `audit_deck_wozniak`, `find_duplicate_cards`.
- **Prompt**: *"Run `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps` on Renal Physiology across every deck: surface related orphan cards, Type 1 missing concepts, Type 2 non-atomic cards, and Type 3 bilingual glue."*

### Stage C — Clean Up Tags and Empty Cards
- **MCP tools**: `audit_tag_hygiene`, `merge_tag_clusters`, `list_empty_cards`, `delete_empty_cards`.
- **Prompt**: *"Audit tag consistency with `audit_tag_hygiene`, merge typo/plural clusters via `merge_tag_clusters`, and check for empty front cards via `list_empty_cards`."*

### Stage D — Batch Split and Refactor Behind the Safeguard
- **MCP tools**: `begin_staged_bundle`, `propose_card_split`, `propose_card_refactor`, `propose_cards_batch_refactor`, `commit_staged_bundle`.
- **Prompt**: *"Start a bundle (`begin_staged_bundle`), split the 8 cards exceeding 40 words into 2–3 atomic notes using `propose_card_split`, tighten vague wording with `propose_card_refactor`, and finalize via `commit_staged_bundle`."*

## 4. Approve in Safeguard and Export Back Without Losing SRS

1. Open **MCP Server & Agents** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>) > **Safeguard & Validation** and review every Before / After split and rewrite visually.
2. Click **Apply** to commit the bundle atomically into AnkiDraft.
3. Export the cleaned deck via <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> (or MCP tool `export_deck_apkg`) and open the `.apkg` in Anki: thanks to stable note GUIDs and [Smart Merge](/en/anki-sync/synchro_smart_merge/), updated wording lands cleanly while preserving your FSRS intervals.

---

# [EN] Zero API Key Workflow: Drive AnkiDraft from Claude or Cursor
URL: https://ankidraft.app/en/workflows/zero-cle-api-agent-mcp/
Description: Connect Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or Cursor to AnkiDraft's local MCP server to generate, enrich, and audit flashcards with two-phase human review.

Already using **Claude Desktop**, **Claude Code**, **Cursor**, or **Antigravity**? Through AnkiDraft's built-in **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** server, you can draft flashcards, audit coverage gaps, and clean up decks with **zero additional API keys** while keeping every edit behind the **Safeguard**.

## 1. Start the Local MCP Server and Copy Client Config

1. Open **MCP Server & Agents** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>) from the sidebar.
2. Confirm the local server shows **Active** on port `8765` (or click **Start**).
3. Under **Ready-to-Use Client Configurations** on the right, pick your client (**Claude**, **Antigravity**, **Cursor**, or **cURL**) and click **Copy Configuration** (or **Open File**).
4. Paste the JSON snippet (`http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp` plus your Bearer token) into your AI client config and restart it.

## 2. Five Concrete MCP Use Cases (Copy-Paste Prompts)

### Case A — Generate Course-Grounded Flashcards by Chapter
- **MCP tools**: `search_document`, `get_document_outline`, `begin_staged_bundle`, `create_notes_batch`, `commit_staged_bundle`.
- **Prompt**: *"Inspect the outline of document #3, read the sections on glycemic regulation with `search_document`, then stage a grouped bundle (`begin_staged_bundle` + `create_notes_batch` + `commit_staged_bundle`) of 12 atomic KaTeX flashcards in deck `Biochemistry::Metabolism`."*

### Case B — Store an External Summary as an Authoritative Source
- **MCP tools**: `write_mcp_artifact`, `ingest_authority_source`, `reindex_document`.
- **Prompt**: *"Write a clean Markdown synthesis of adaptive immunity from my lecture notes, save it with `write_mcp_artifact`, and ingest it with `ingest_authority_source` so newly generated cards keep section-level provenance links."*

### Case C — Create or Modernize Note Types and Card CSS
- **MCP tools**: `list_note_types`, `get_note_type_details`, `propose_note_type_refactor`, `propose_css_tune`, `preview_card_render`.
- **Prompt**: *"Inspect the `Medical Cloze` note type via `get_note_type_details`, improve hint contrast in dark mode with `propose_css_tune`, check the output using `preview_card_render`, and stage `propose_note_type_refactor` for Safeguard approval."*

### Case D — Run a DAG Pipeline in Delegated MCP Mode
- **MCP tools**: `list_pipelines`, `trigger_pipeline_run`, `provide_pipeline_step_content`.
- **Prompt**: *"List my pipelines via `list_pipelines`, start pipeline #2 in delegated mode with `trigger_pipeline_run`, supply each paused step output via `provide_pipeline_step_content`, and send the resulting cards to the Safeguard."*

### Case E — Clean Up and Refactor Existing Decks
- **MCP tools**: `get_flagged_cards`, `diagnose_domain_knowledge_gaps`, `propose_card_split`, `propose_card_refactor`.
- **Prompt**: *"Fetch my red-flagged cards with `get_flagged_cards` and split dense cards into atomic prompts with `propose_card_split`."* (See [Anki Collection Rescue & MCP Hygiene](/en/workflows/sauvetage-et-hygiene-anki-mcp/)).

## 3. Review and Approve in the Safeguard (Two-Phase Commit)

Nothing is written behind your back:
1. Open the **Safeguard & Validation** sub-tab under **MCP Server & Agents** (<kbd>Alt+5</kbd>).
2. Review the **Before / After semantic diff**, live HTML/KaTeX card preview, and deletion or split impact.
3. Click **Apply** to commit the bundle atomically into SQLite, or **Reject** to discard every change cleanly.

---

# [FR] Consultant IA et Connexion aux Assistants MCP
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/ai-setup/consultant_mcp/
Description: Discutez avec le Consultant IA intégré ou connectez Claude Desktop et Cursor à AnkiDraft via MCP pour auditer et enrichir vos paquets facilement.

Le **Consultant IA** (<kbd>Ctrl+6</kbd>) est votre assistant pédagogique au sein d'AnkiDraft. Vous pouvez également piloter AnkiDraft depuis votre client IA externe favori grâce au protocole standard **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**.

## 1. Ce que le Consultant IA peut faire pour vous

Posez-lui vos demandes en langage naturel :
- *« Trouve les chapitres de mon cours de cardiologie qui n'ont pas encore de cartes »*
- *« Cherche les doublons dans mon paquet Anatomie et propose une fusion »*
- *« Raccourcis les 10 cartes les plus longues de ce paquet selon les règles de Wozniak »*

## 2. Garde-fou de sécurité : validation humaine en deux temps

Ni le Consultant IA intégré ni un agent externe connecté via MCP ne peut modifier ou supprimer vos cartes sans votre accord :
1. L'assistant prépare ses modifications dans un **lot en attente (Staged Bundle)**.
2. Vous visualisez clairement l'avant/après de chaque carte ajoutée, modifiée ou supprimée.
3. Vous cliquez sur **Appliquer** ou **Rejeter** : vous gardez toujours le contrôle absolu sur votre collection.

## 3. Connecter un client externe (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.)

Dans la vue **Consultant IA** > **Serveur MCP**, activez le serveur local et copiez la configuration en un clic pour permettre à votre assistant externe d'interroger vos paquets et vos cours en toute sécurité.

# [FR] Configurer vos Fournisseurs d'IA (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/ai-setup/ia_fournisseurs/
Description: Connectez vos clés API OpenAI, Anthropic ou Gemini en toute sécurité, configurez vos modèles locaux et maîtrisez votre budget de tokens IA global.

AnkiDraft est **agnostique du fournisseur d'IA** : vous êtes libre d'utiliser le service de votre choix ou d'alterner selon vos besoins.

## 1. Fournisseurs compatibles

Dans **Paramètres** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Fournisseurs IA**, vous pouvez configurer :
- **OpenAI** (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, etc.)
- **Google Gemini** (Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro)
- **Anthropic Claude** (Claude Sonnet, Claude Haiku)
- **Tout serveur compatible OpenAI** (Mistral, OpenRouter, serveur universitaire local)
- **Ollama (100 % gratuit et hors ligne)** : voir le guide [Utiliser un Modèle Local avec Ollama](/fr/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/).

## 2. Sécurité de vos clés API

- Vos clés API sont enregistrées dans le **trousseau sécurisé de votre système d'exploitation** (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service Linux).
- Elles ne transitent par aucun serveur intermédiaire : AnkiDraft communique directement depuis votre ordinateur vers l'API du fournisseur sélectionné.
- Les journaux techniques masquent automatiquement toute clé (`sk-*`, `AIza*`).

## 3. Contrôle du budget

Avant de lancer une génération importante sur un livre entier, AnkiDraft estime le nombre de jetons (*tokens*) nécessaires et vous permet de fixer un plafond par exécution pour éviter toute surprise de facturation.

# [FR] Utiliser un Modèle Local Gratuit avec Ollama
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/ai-setup/local-models-ollama/
Description: Générez des flashcards Anki atomiques 100 % hors-ligne et gratuitement sur votre ordinateur grâce aux modèles locaux Ollama sans aucune clé API.

Vous ne souhaitez pas utiliser d'API payante ou vous étudiez des documents confidentiels sans connexion internet ? AnkiDraft s'intègre nativement avec **Ollama**.

## 1. Installer Ollama en 2 minutes

1. Téléchargez et installez Ollama depuis [ollama.com](https://ollama.com).
2. Ouvrez un terminal et téléchargez un modèle adapté à la configuration de votre ordinateur :
   - **Ordinateur avec 8 Go de RAM** : `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` ou `ollama pull qwen2.5:3b`
   - **Ordinateur avec 16 Go+ de RAM (ex. Mac M1/M2/M3/M4)** : `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` ou `ollama pull mistral`

## 2. Activer Ollama dans AnkiDraft

1. Ouvrez **Paramètres** (<kbd>Ctrl+,</kbd>) > **Fournisseurs IA**.
2. Sélectionnez **Ollama (Local)** : l'adresse par défaut `http://localhost:11434` est détectée automatiquement.
3. Cliquez sur **Rafraîchir les modèles** et choisissez le modèle que vous venez de télécharger.
4. Vous pouvez désormais générer et auditer vos flashcards gratuitement et 100 % hors ligne !

# [FR] Exporter vos Paquets vers Anki (.apkg)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/anki-sync/export-apkg/
Description: Générez un fichier .apkg propre et prêt à réviser pour Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb et AnkiMobile avec IDs stables et sans perdre votre historique.

Une fois vos cartes créées et relues dans AnkiDraft, vous pouvez les transférer vers Anki en quelques secondes grâce à l'export `.apkg`.

## 1. Exporter un paquet ou une sélection

1. Appuyez sur <kbd>Ctrl+Alt+E</kbd> ou cliquez sur **Exporter (.apkg)** dans la barre d'outils.
2. Choisissez le paquet (ou les sous-paquets hiérarchiques `Matière::Chapitre`) à exporter.
3. Cochez **Inclure les fichiers médias** si vos cartes contiennent des schémas, des images ou de l'audio TTS.
4. Cliquez sur **Exporter** et choisissez l'emplacement du fichier `.apkg`.

## 2. Ouvrir le paquet dans Anki sans écraser vos révisions

Double-cliquez sur le fichier `.apkg` généré :
- Chaque carte possède un **identifiant unique durable (GUID)**.
- Si vous réexportez un paquet après avoir corrigé une faute d'orthographe dans AnkiDraft, Anki met à jour le texte de la carte **tout en conservant intact votre historique de révision FSRS / SM-2** (intervalles, échéances, facteur de facilité).
- Les drapeaux de couleur (*flags*) et l'état suspendu de vos cartes sont également respectés.

---

# [FR] Importer un Paquet (.apkg) ou une Collection (.colpkg)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/anki-sync/import-colpkg/
Description: Chargez vos paquets Anki .apkg ou .colpkg existants dans AnkiDraft pour les enrichir, auditer leur qualité et suivre votre couverture de cours.

Vous utilisez déjà Anki depuis des mois ou des années ? Vous pouvez importer vos cartes existantes dans AnkiDraft à tout moment.

## 1. Ouvrir l'assistant d'importation (<kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd>)

Appuyez sur <kbd>Ctrl+Shift+I</kbd> et glissez votre fichier : AnkiDraft reconnaît automatiquement s'il s'agit d'un paquet `.apkg` ou d'une collection complète `.colpkg`.

## 2. Différence entre `.apkg` et `.colpkg`

- **Paquet `.apkg` (ajout ou fusion ciblée)** : ajoute les cartes d'un cours partagé par un camarade ou met à jour un paquet spécifique sans toucher au reste de votre collection.
- **Archive `.colpkg` (synchronisation complète depuis Anki)** : aligne l'intégralité de vos paquets, types de notes et compteurs de révision sur votre collection Anki actuelle, tout en préservant vos PDF, vos réglages et vos assistants IA dans AnkiDraft.

Pour visualiser en détail l'articulation entre AnkiDraft et Anki, consultez le [Guide Visuel du Cycle de Vie Distribué](/fr/guides/cycle_de_vie_distribue/).

---

# [FR] Synchronisation, Doublons et Fusion Intelligente (Smart Merge)
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/anki-sync/synchro_smart_merge/
Description: Résolvez les conflits lors d'un import Anki avec le Smart Merge, préservez votre historique de révision et éliminez les cartes en doublon facilement.

Lorsque vous travaillez à plusieurs sur un même paquet ou que vous modifiez une carte à la fois dans Anki et dans AnkiDraft, l'outil de **Fusion Intelligente (Smart Merge)** protège votre travail.

## 1. Comment fonctionne Smart Merge lors d'un import `.apkg` ?

Si une carte entrante possède le même identifiant qu'une carte déjà présente dans AnkiDraft :
- **Si seules les statistiques de révision ont changé dans Anki** : aucun conflit n'est déclenché, la mise à jour est transparente.
- **Si le texte de la carte a été modifié des deux côtés** : la fenêtre de comparaison à 3 panneaux (*Version locale*, *Base commune*, *Version importée*) s'ouvre pour vous permettre de choisir la formulation à conserver ou de combiner les deux.

## 2. Détecter et fusionner les doublons

Depuis l'éditeur ou via le Consultant IA, vous pouvez lancer une recherche de doublons sur vos paquets :
- **Doublons exacts** : cartes ayant le même recto.
- **Doublons proches** : cartes formulées légèrement différemment mais portant sur la même définition, détectées rapidement grâce au calcul de similarité intégré.

---

# [FR] Générer des Flashcards avec l'IA
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/cards/ai-generation/
Description: Transformez automatiquement un chapitre de cours en flashcards Questions/Réponses ou textes à trous atomiques avec validation humaine stricte.

AnkiDraft vous aide à transformer rapidement un chapitre dense en flashcards atomiques, tout en vous laissant le dernier mot sur chaque carte grâce à la revue humaine.

## 1. Lancer une génération par lot

1. Ouvrez la vue **Génération** (<kbd>Ctrl+4</kbd>) ou cliquez sur **Générer des cartes** depuis un document.
2. Choisissez les sections du cours à traiter dans le compositeur de lots (**Batch Slice Composer**) :
   - **Mode Direct** : chaque section cochée produit un lot de cartes dédié.
   - **Mode Automatique** : regroupe ou divise les sections selon leur longueur.
3. Sélectionnez le type de carte souhaité (*Basique Recto/Verso*, *Texte à trous / Cloze*) ainsi que le paquet Anki de destination.
4. Appuyez sur <kbd>Ctrl+Entrée</kbd> pour démarrer la génération.

## 2. Personnaliser le style des cartes (Personas)

Vous pouvez adapter le ton et l'exigence de l'IA selon votre domaine d'étude :
- **Sciences & Médecine** : définitions précises, mécanismes physiopathologiques, valeurs de référence.
- **Droit & Sciences humaines** : notions clés, distinctions conceptuelles, dates et arrêts.
- **Langues & Vocabulaire** : exemples contextualisés, expressions idiomatiques et prononciation.

## 3. Revue humaine avant enregistrement (Staging)

Aucune carte générée par l'IA n'est ajoutée aveuglément à votre collection : toutes les propositions arrivent dans la file de **Revue (Staging)** où vous pouvez les accepter, les modifier ou les rejeter en un clic.

---

# [FR] Synthèse Vocale (TTS) et Cartes Audio
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/cards/audio-tts/
Description: Générez automatiquement une prononciation audio naturelle hors-ligne pour vos cartes de langues et terminologies avec les voix Kokoro ou Piper.

Pour l'apprentissage des langues étrangères, de la médecine ou de la musique, associer un extrait sonore à une flashcard renforce considérablement la mémorisation.

## 1. Générer la prononciation d'un champ en un clic

1. Dans l'éditeur de notes, placez votre curseur dans le champ contenant le mot ou la phrase à prononcer.
2. Cliquez sur l'icône **Synthèse vocale (TTS)** dans la barre d'outils.
3. Choisissez la langue et la voix naturelle souhaitée (français, anglais, espagnol, allemand, japonais, mandarin, etc.).
4. Le fichier audio est généré, normalisé et attaché automatiquement à votre carte sous la forme `[sound:fichier.mp3]` compatible avec Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb et AnkiMobile.

## 2. Génération audio en lot

Vous avez un paquet entier de vocabulaire sans audio ? Sélectionnez plusieurs cartes dans la table d'édition et lancez la **Génération TTS par lot** : AnkiDraft sonorise toutes les cartes sélectionnées en arrière-plan.

# [FR] Pipelines de Génération et Couverture Intelligente
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/cards/dag_et_rag/
Description: Automatisez la création de cartes par étapes avec les pipelines DAG et comblez les lacunes de vos cours grâce au RAG local et Smart Coverage.

Pour les cours volumineux, AnkiDraft combine deux moteurs complémentaires : les **Pipelines de génération** (workflows DAG) et la **Couverture intelligente** (RAG & Smart Coverage).

## 1. Enchaîner plusieurs étapes automatiquement (Pipeline DAG)

Un pipeline vous permet d'enchaîner automatiquement plusieurs actions sur vos chapitres :
1. **Recherche des passages clés** dans votre cours.
2. **Extraction des flashcards** selon le modèle de carte choisi.
3. **Vérification qualité automatique** (filtrage des cartes trop longues) et **génération audio TTS**.
4. **Passage en revue humaine** avant validation finale.

## 2. Détecter les chapitres oubliés (Smart Coverage)

Grâce à l'indexation sémantique locale de vos documents et aux liens de provenance (`NoteChunkLinkModel`), AnkiDraft compare vos cartes existantes à l'intégralité de votre cours :
- Il met en évidence les sections qui ne possèdent encore aucune flashcard.
- Vous pouvez demander à l'IA de **générer uniquement les cartes manquantes** sans dupliquer celles que vous avez déjà créées.

---

# [FR] Éditeur de Notes, Formules KaTeX et Textes à Trous
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/cards/editeur_notes_katex/
Description: Rédigez et mettez en forme vos flashcards avec aperçu mathématique KaTeX en direct, occlusions Cloze, médias et historique complet des révisions.

L'éditeur de notes d'AnkiDraft (<kbd>Ctrl+2</kbd>) vous offre un confort d'écriture immédiat avec prévisualisation en temps réel du rendu Anki.

## 1. Écrire des formules mathématiques et chimiques (KaTeX)

AnkiDraft affiche instantanément vos équations LaTeX sans attendre l'export vers Anki :
- **Formule en ligne** : entourez votre expression de `\( ... \)` ou `$ ... $` (ex. `$E = mc^2$`).
- **Formule en bloc centré** : utilisez `\[ ... \]` ou `$$ ... $$`.
- **Autocomplétion LaTeX** : tapez `\` suivi des premières lettres d'un symbole (`\alpha`, `\frac`, `\sum`) pour afficher la liste des commandes disponibles.

## 2. Créer des textes à trous (Cloze)

Les cartes à trous sont idéales pour mémoriser une définition précise ou une énumération courte :
1. Sélectionnez le mot ou l'expression à masquer dans votre texte.
2. Appuyez sur le bouton **Cloze** de la barre d'outils pour insérer automatiquement `{{c1::votre texte}}`.
3. Vous pouvez ajouter un indice optionnel avec la syntaxe `{{c1::réponse::indice}}`.

## 3. Historique de révision (Time Machine)

Vous avez modifié une carte par erreur ? Chaque enregistrement (<kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd>) conserve une version dans l'historique local de la note : vous pouvez comparer et restaurer une formulation antérieure en un clic.

---

# [FR] Audit Qualité et les 20 Règles de Wozniak
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/cards/linter_wozniak/
Description: Détectez et scindez les cartes trop longues, floues ou difficiles à mémoriser grâce au Linter des 20 règles de Wozniak pour mieux retenir durablement.

Une mauvaise flashcard (trop longue, contenant plusieurs questions à la fois ou dépourvue de contexte) finit par devenir une « sangsue » (*leech*) que vous oubliez sans cesse dans Anki.

AnkiDraft intègre un **Linter pédagogique** inspiré des **20 règles de formulation des connaissances de Piotr Wozniak** (créateur de SuperMemo).

## 1. Ce que vérifie l'audit qualité

Dans la vue **Qualité & Audit** (<kbd>Ctrl+5</kbd>) ou directement dans l'éditeur, AnkiDraft attribue un score de santé à chaque carte et signale :
- **La surcharge d'information (non-atomicité)** : une réponse qui dépasse le seuil recommandé ou qui mélange plusieurs idées distinctes.
- **Les questions vagues ou ambiguës** : questions ouvertes du type *« Parlez de… »* qui ne permettent pas de savoir quelle réponse précise est attendue.
- **Les énumérations aveugles** : listes de plus de 3 ou 4 éléments difficiles à restituer dans l'ordre.
- **Les cartes à trous trop larges** : clozes qui masquent une phrase entière au lieu d'un concept précis.

## 2. Scinder une carte complexe en un clic

Lorsqu'une carte est signalée comme trop dense, cliquez sur **Scinder en cartes atomiques** : l'assistant vous propose de la découper en 2 ou 3 cartes courtes et indépendantes, beaucoup plus faciles à mémoriser sur le long terme.

---

# [FR] Modèles de Cartes, Gabarits et Styles CSS
URL: https://ankidraft.app/fr/cards/note-types-and-templates/
Description: Personnalisez vos types de notes Recto/Verso et Cloze, vos gabarits Jinja2 et votre mise en forme CSS pour Anki Desktop, AnkiWeb et AnkiMobile.

AnkiDraft prend en charge tous les types de notes d'Anki et vous permet d'adapter leur présentation visuelle.

## 1. Les types de notes prêts à l'emploi

- **Basique (Recto / Verso)** : une question ciblée au recto, la réponse et un mémo de cours optionnel au verso.
- **Basique (et carte inversée)** : génère automatiquement la carte dans les deux sens (idéal pour le vocabulaire bilingue).
- **Texte à trous (Cloze)** : masque un ou plusieurs termes clés `{{c1::...}}` au sein d'une phrase de contexte.

## 2. Personnaliser les champs et le style CSS

Vous pouvez ajouter des champs personnalisés (ex. *Source*, *Moyen mnémotechnique*, *Audio*, *Illustration*) et ajuster la feuille de style CSS de vos cartes avec un aperçu immédiat en mode clair et en mode sombre.

## 3. Réconciliation intelligente à l'import

Lorsque vous importez un paquet `.apkg` contenant un type de note déjà présent dans votre collection, AnkiDraft le reconnaît automatiquement sans créer de doublon de modèle (`Basique-12345`).
